input: The driver describes no witnessed loss of consciousness but sometimes feels light-headed when standing quickly.

The driver's mother has diabetes and uses insulin, but the driver says there has been no diagnosis of diabetes for him; he has recently felt thirsty and noticed intermittent blur, and a laboratory appointment has been arranged.
An undated eye card lists 6/12 and 6/9 without identifying the eyes or correction status.
The driver thinks the blur improves after resting, but current acuity, fields and the presence of true diplopia have not been established.
The nurse distinguishes family history and provisional questions from confirmed patient findings.

He describes a brief blank sensation after poor sleep but remembers the whole conversation, while a colleague says he paused before replying; there is no confirmed loss of consciousness and no specialist determination of a cause.

A borrowed glucose meter produced an isolated elevated value without a verified technique or accompanying clinical assessment, so neither a diagnosis nor a treatment category has been established from the available material.
